:::{#def-two-part-description-length}
#### Two-part description length

Let $x$ be data,
and let $\modelfam$ be a finite set of models,
each of which gives $x$ a [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $p(x)$.
Let a [prefix code](huffman-codes.qmd#def-prefix-code) on $\modelfam$ give each model $p$ a codeword of $L(p)$ [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit).

The **two-part description length** of $x$ under a model $p$ is

$$L(p) + \log_2 \frac{1}{p(x)}.$$

The first part is the length of the codeword that names the model.
The second part is the [surprisal](entropy.qmd#def-surprisal) of $x$ under the model,
which is the length in bits of a code for $x$ built from the model.

:::
